concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: The original DPA breach clause requires notification within 48 hours, and the amendment changing this to 24 hours only takes effect on 1 October 2026, after 15 September 2026.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment replacing the breach clause with a 24-hour notification limit took effect on 1 October 2026, so it governs on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment reducing the on-site audit notice period from 30 days to 20 days took effect on 1 October 2026, so it applies on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amended liability clause, effective 1 October 2026, caps the Processor's aggregate liability for breaches of the DPA at EUR 1,000,000 regardless of fees paid.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The amended liability clause expressly states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap does not apply to breaches of the confidentiality section.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed as an approved Sub-processor in the DPA annex, and its withdrawal only takes effect on 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: The approval of Meridian Mail Ltd was withdrawn with effect from 1 January 2027, so it is no longer an approved Sub-processor on 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: Processing as of 1 February 2027 occurs in Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, France and Denmark, based on the approved Sub-processors and the data-location statements, with Ireland excluded after the Meridian withdrawal.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: Under the amended return and deletion clause in force on 31 December 2026, the 60-day period runs from 31 December 2026 to 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, and the notice must describe the breach's nature, affected data, likely consequences and measures taken.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting data processed under the DPA, and the notice must describe the breach's nature, affected data, likely consequences and measures taken.
justifications: The amended breach clause in force on 1 November 2026 sets the 24-hour outer limit, and the unchanged content requirements remain applicable.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: The breach was confirmed to expose usable privileged credentials, so the 12-hour expedited outer limit applies, measured from the original awareness and not reset by the later credential confirmation.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: The 12-hour expedited limit from original awareness at 17:10 on 9 April 2027 expired at 05:10 on 10 April, and the first notice was delivered at 06:00, 50 minutes later.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: Awareness on Friday 9 April is followed by Business Days 13, 15 and 16 April, since 12 April is a closure date and the Controller approved only 14 April as a pause, so the third Business Day ends on 16 April.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: Held ORD records must be deleted by the later of the 60-day ordinary deadline (29 August 2027) and the tenth Business Day after the last hold ends on 25 August 2027, which is 9 September 2027. The 30 August closure date is excluded from the business-day count.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: BK-0630 was created on 30 June 2027 and contains no held records, so it must be deleted by the earlier of its ordinary deadline and 35 calendar days after creation, which is 4 August 2027. The restoration does not restart this period.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: After termination, records retained under a legal hold may be used only for legal preservation, and the Controller rejected the analytics retention request. The hold has ended but the deletion window following its release remains the sole retention authority, so no service delivery or analytics use is permitted.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Conditional approval for expanded processing from 1 March 2027 begins no earlier than the latest of the proposed start date, security review completion, and written consent. For the Stockholm service, the security review completed last, on 22 April.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS was added as an approved Sub-processor for transactional email from 1 January 2027 and continues that service on 10 May 2027. The emergency permission for Meridian Mail Ltd is limited to incident notices and does not authorise ordinary customer email.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: These countries have ongoing processing (Norway storage, Estonia and Lithuania hosting and monitoring, France email, Sweden Stockholm infrastructure) with effective authorisation on 15 May 2027. Ireland, Denmark, Finland and Germany are excluded because their authorisation was withdrawn, expired, or never took effect.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: The security cap is the greater of EUR 2,000,000 and twice Qualifying Fees, which total EUR 1,140,000 after excluding VAT, the service credit, and training fees, giving EUR 2,280,000.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap of EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year less the EUR 300,000 ordinary payments already made in the current Contract Year leaves EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: Claim C-1 is payable up to the remaining ordinary pool of EUR 700,000, L-2 is payable in full as security (EUR 1,750,000) within the remaining security pool, and L-3 and L-4 are uncapped confidentiality losses (EUR 250,000 and EUR 100,000), totaling EUR 2,800,000.
